s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with recent systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
key_facts: Teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Neurological complications
Recently acquired periorbital hyperpigmentation
Ocular history negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis had been ruled out
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OU
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis
Aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus
Positive IgM CHIKV serologic test

differentials: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute posterior multifocal placoid pigment epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Chikungunya virus ocular infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive IgM CHIKV serologic test and aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus

shortlist.label: Post-viral immune-mediated interstitial keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent systemic symptoms and bilateral ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and absence of trauma or previous inflammation

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ocular inflammation and recent systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of bilateral blurred vision, ocular irritation, and recent history of fever and arthralgia, combined with the positive aqueous tap PCR results for Chikungunya virus and positive IgM CHIKV serologic test, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Post-viral immune-mediated interstitial keratitis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of viral infection, the specific findings of Chikungunya virus in the aqueous tap PCR and the clinical presentation point more directly to a Chikungunya virus ocular infection.

rejected.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with heterochromia of the iris and chronic uveitis, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
rejected.why: The aqueous tap PCR results were negative for human herpesviruses 1 and 2, ruling out this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus keratitis
rejected.why: The aqueous tap PCR results were negative for varicella-zoster virus, making this diagnosis unlikely.
